The video intercuts the live scene with popular meme reaction shots—including a man with text 'khao maa kasam panipuri,' a 'WAIT' face, a man adjusting sunglasses, a woman singing, and an audience face-palming—to amplify the comedy. The tone is lighthearted and playful, typical of Indian street-food skit content, ending with the girl explaining her reasoning up close to the camera.

The comedy is amplified by the children's earnest wrong answer, the vendor's exaggerated reactions, and inserted popular reaction memes ('WAIT', facepalm crowd) that signal mock disbelief. description:
A male creator wearing a green Von Dutch t-shirt, glasses, and a backward brown cap reviews a snack called the 'Dubai Chewy Cookie' from Yayank Dessert. He introduces it as a legendary snack for 2050, noting this version uses Dancow milk powder instead of the more common chocolate version. In close-up shots, he breaks open the pale, round cookie to reveal a bright green, textured pistachio-kunafa filling that fills the interior completely. He describes the outer skin as thin and chewy, not overly thick, and points out that the green filling is visible through the skin. After tasting it, he says the first flavor is a clear milky aroma from the Dancow, followed by a satisfying crunch from the kunafa. He states that according to him, a good kunafa spread needs a salty/savory note, which this has. He compares it to the chocolate version, saying the chocolate is more balanced and his personal favorite, while the Dancow/milky version will suit people who like a sweet, milky taste paired with the savory kunafa. He concludes by recommending viewers try it themselves.
